Lauren and team — I agree with the split. As the bar-raiser, I'm adding a short appendix of leveling expectations and red flags so we have consistent scoring during debrief. High-level summary below (I also attached a one-page note).

Leveling expectations (L6 vs L7):
- L6 (Senior): owns one or more production surfaces end-to-end, consistently drives API/infra improvements, mentors others, requires some direction on cross-org initiatives but can drive a feature/major incident triage independently.
- L7 (Principal): recognized cross-org leader on infra strategy, sets SLOs/cost targets, drives migration/large rollout plans, shapes hiring & technical strategy.

Bar-raiser focus areas (what I will assess):
- Depth of decision-making: can the candidate explain trade-offs with data and consequences (latency, cost, operational complexity)?
- Incident posture: concrete examples where they led incident resolution, postmortems, and systemic fixes.
- People influence: examples of convincing stakeholders, building consensus, and lifting teams.

Hard fail signals:
- Only academic/research experience with no production deployment evidence
- Vague or inconsistent answers on root cause/mitigation during real incidents
- Inability to articulate trade-offs (e.g., says "we just shard more" without cost or complexity framing)

Scoring guidance: use a 1–5 scale per area (system design, runtime perf, leadership, ownership). A pass requires minimum average 3.5 and no area below 3.

I'll be strict on evidence — ask follow-ups that force specificity. If you want, I can host a 10-minute pre-interview calibration call the morning of Wed (10–10:10 PT).

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
